item.title: IMF-World Bank jobs agenda underscores relevance of FirstBank’s SME financing
item.description: By Babajide Komolafe, Economy Editor There is a growing global challenge of job creation, and the need to accelerate private-sector investment, particularly through micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs), featured prominently at the just-concluded 2026 Annual Meetings of the World Bank Group and the International Monetary Fund (IMF) in Bangkok, Thailand. Discussions at the august gathering of finance ministers and central bank governors, among other participants, underscored the importance of small businesses in expanding economic activity, creating employment and improving livelihoods, placing access to finance and business support at the centre of efforts to achieve sustainable growth. The World Bank Group President, Ajay Banga, underscored the importance of small businesses to the global economy, describing them as “the engine of the economy”. According to Banga, MSMEs represent 90 per cent of firms and employ 75 per cent of workers in developing countries. “Job creation is not automatic. It comes from businesses that can start, that can grow, that can hire, that can trade, and that can compete,” he said at the Bank’s October 13 session on MSME financing and job creation. The scale of the challenge was further highlighted by projections that about 1.2 billion young people in developing countries would reach working age over the next 10 to 15 years, while only about 420 million jobs were expected to be created. The employment gap, according to the World Bank Group, makes it imperative for governments and development institutions to mobilise private investment and support businesses capable of expanding production and generating jobs. The IMF Managing Director, Kristalina Georgieva, also called for improvements in the business environment, stronger competition and investment in digital and energy infrastructure as part of measures to strengthen economic performance. “For governments it means improving the business environment, strengthening competition. Investing in digital and energy infrastructure and embracing active labor market policies,” Georgieva said at the IMF’s October 14 Global Policy Agenda briefing. For Nigeria, where small businesses operate across trade, agriculture, manufacturing, professional services and other sectors, the discussions underscore the importance of financing viable enterprises and strengthening their capacity to grow. The issue also brings into focus the role of commercial banks in providing the credit, payment infrastructure, digital services and business support required by small enterprises to expand their operations. Financing the SME sector FirstBank of Nigeria’s disbursement of more than N200 billion to small businesses in 2024 provides an example of the financing role commercial banks can play in supporting the sector. item.title: Fountain of Life board reaffirms Jimmy Odukoya’s removal, names Okpaise interim leader
item.description: The Board of Trustees of Fountain of Life Church has reaffirmed its decision to remove Pastor Jimmy Odukoya as senior pastor, appointing Pastor Rotimi Okpaise to oversee the church’s interim spiritual and administrative leadership. The board said the interim arrangement would remain in force pending consultations and the completion of processes for appointing a substantive leadership structure in accordance with the church’s constitution and established procedures. The latest decision comes amid an escalating leadership and succession dispute between the board and Jimmy, son of the church’s late founder, Pastor Taiwo Odukoya, who had earlier rejected his removal. In a statement on Tuesday, the trustees insisted that their November 16, 2026 resolution withdrawing recognition of Jimmy as senior pastor remained valid. The board also alleged that individuals linked to Jimmy had taken control of the church’s social media platforms without its authorisation and were using them to publish what it described as inaccurate and misleading accounts of the dispute. “The Board stands by its earlier statement in its entirety, and its resolution of 16 November 2026 remains in force,” it said. The trustees explained that the decision followed a review of the church’s leadership and succession arrangements, as well as what they described as longstanding governance concerns and current doctrinal and moral controversies. They said Jimmy had previously been asked to step down before the board resolved to withdraw its recognition of him as senior pastor with immediate effect. “He is required to step down forthwith from the office and all functions of Senior Pastor,” the statement added. The board said the decision was intended to create an atmosphere conducive to restoring peace, rebuilding trust and resolving the church’s leadership and governance challenges. It stressed that the action was not motivated by vindictiveness, humiliation or personal condemnation but was considered necessary to protect the church’s spiritual heritage, institutional integrity and public reputation. The trustees also warned that statements appearing on the church’s social media platforms should not be regarded as official positions of the board. They said only statements issued and signed on behalf of the board should be recognised as official, adding that steps were being taken to restore the church’s communication channels to authorised control. Background to succession dispute Providing details of the succession disagreement, the board said Fountain of Life Church had built its reputation over three decades on biblical truth, sound doctrine, spiritual integrity and Christian leadership under its founding pastors. It said responsibility for ensuring an orderly leadership transition rested with the board following the death of Taiwo Odukoya in 2023. item.title: ECOWAS court president seeks improved justice delivery, harmonised judicial standards
item.description: By Innocent Anaba The President of the Community Court of Justice of the Economic Community of West African States, ECOWAS, Justice Charlyne Brumskine, has called for stronger institutional collaboration, harmonised judicial practices and improved justice delivery across the West African sub-region. Brumskine made the call while declaring open the Court’s 2026 Judicial Retreat in Niger State, Nigeria. She described the five-day retreat as an important opportunity for judges and judicial support staff to review existing practices, address emerging institutional challenges and develop strategies for improving the administration of justice. The ECOWAS Court president said the retreat was taking place at a critical stage in the institution’s development, following the adoption of a harmonised legal framework under Supplementary Act SA.1/12/25, the deployment of the Electronic Case Management System, ECMS, and the commencement of the implementation of the Court’s Strategic Plan 2026–2030. She noted that the first strategic goal of the plan was to guarantee timely and impartial justice. According to her, the developments require clear and harmonised institutional standards to ensure that the Court’s legal framework, technological infrastructure and judicial practices work together effectively. “Our task this week is to build on that foundation, consolidate the best practices and experiences, and improve upon the standards where needed,” she said. Brumskine stressed the importance of collaboration among the Judges’ Chambers, the Registry, the Research and Documentation Department and other support departments, noting that effective judicial administration depended on the collective efforts of all units. “It is our collective responsibility to build a Court whose standards, systems and procedures consistently support judicial independence, efficiency, accountability and public confidence,” she added. Earlier, the acting Deputy Chief Registrar of the Court, Mrs. Marie Saine, outlined the objectives and expected outcomes of the retreat. She said the overall objective was to adopt harmonised standards, guidelines and working procedures to promote the effective and efficient administration of justice. Saine identified the adoption of standardised judgment templates, a judgment-drafting style guide and quality-assurance procedures, as well as the establishment of an Editorial Committee, among the key objectives. Others include strengthening legal research support and collaboration between the Judges’ Chambers and the Research and Documentation Department. She said the retreat would also consider the 2027 judicial calendar, external court sessions, guidelines for virtual sittings and priorities for further development of the Electronic Case Management System. The review and determination of Instructions to the Chief Registrar and Practice Directions are also expected to form part of the deliberations. item.title: Troops arrest seven suspects, recover 38 phones in Jos
item.description: By Golok Nanmwa JOS – Troops of Sector One, Operation Enduring Peace (OPEP), have arrested seven suspected criminals and recovered 38 mobile phones and other suspected stolen items during separate operations in Jos North Local Government Area of Plateau State. The operations, involving troops deployed in Jos and Naraguta, also led to the recovery of a suspected stolen motorcycle, a toy pistol and a Mercedes-Benz E350 car. Parading the suspects before journalists, the Media and Information Officer of OPEP, Captain Polycarp Oteh, said the first operation followed a report of phone-snatching at gunpoint on November 6, 2026. He said the report led troops to Prime House Hotel along Ring Road, Jos, where five suspects were arrested. Oteh identified them as Tahir Suleiman, 25; Muhammed Ahmed, 25; Muhammed Labaran Haruna, 27; Yahya Yunusa, 20; and Aisha Mohammad, 22. Items recovered during the operation included 38 mobile phones, 27 phone pouches, three MP3 devices, two earpods, an HP laptop, four smartwatches, a dagger, four power banks and a Mercedes-Benz E350 with registration number Plateau BBK-01NB. He said the operation was in line with the mandate of the Commander, Operation Enduring Peace, Maj. Gen. W.M. Dangana, to sustain peace and security across Plateau State, particularly during the yuletide season. The OPEP spokesman further disclosed that troops deployed at Naraguta, working with members of the Vigilante Group of Nigeria (VGN), arrested two additional suspects during a routine patrol. He identified them as Mudasiru Ishaq, 27, and Hasiya Sani, 22, adding that they were allegedly found in possession of a suspected stolen Boxer motorcycle and a toy pistol. Oteh said all seven suspects, alongside the recovered items, would be handed over to the Plateau State Police Command for further investigation and possible prosecution. “These operational successes underscore the commitment of the Commander of Operation Enduring Peace, Maj. Gen. W.M. Dangana, to combating criminal activities while ensuring the safety of lives and property within its Joint Operations Area,” he said. He reiterated the commander’s directive for sustained intelligence-driven operations and effective collaboration with other security agencies and local vigilante groups to deny criminal elements freedom of action. Oteh urged members of the public to remain vigilant and provide credible and timely information to security agencies to support ongoing efforts to restore and sustain peace in Plateau State. item.title: ADC to INEC: Don’t tamper with our leadership, candidates
item.description: …files 17 grounds of appeal against Lifu’s judgment By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – The African Democratic Congress (ADC) has asked the Court of Appeal to restrain the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) from altering its leadership records and the nomination particulars of its presidential and governorship candidates pending the determination of its challenge to a judgment by Justice Peter Lifu of the Federal High Court, Abuja. The party is seeking to stop INEC from implementing a judgment it considers legally defective, arguing that any changes to its leadership records or candidates’ particulars before the appeal is decided could undermine the outcome of the proceedings and jeopardise its preparations for the 2027 elections. In a statement by the Director of Strategic Communication of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, Phrank Shaibu, the party said its 17-ground Notice of Appeal challenged the trial court’s jurisdiction to entertain what it described as an internal party leadership dispute. It also questioned the treatment of an earlier Federal High Court judgment delivered on July 2, 2026, concerning its leadership transition, which it maintained remained valid and had not been set aside. “The 17 grounds challenge the foundation, findings and orders of Justice Lifu’s judgment. The ADC has asked the Court of Appeal to examine whether the trial court had jurisdiction, whether the claimant had standing, whether disputed evidence was properly assessed, and whether the sweeping orders made against the party can stand in law,” Shaibu said. Beyond the substantive appeal, the ADC is separately challenging a July 24, 2026, ruling which granted Hon. Nafiu Bala Gombe leave to amend his originating summons despite the party’s pending preliminary objection to the trial court’s jurisdiction. In its appellant’s brief, the party argued that the court ought to have determined the jurisdictional objection before considering Gombe’s application to amend the suit. It further contended that the proposed amendment altered the description of parties and the capacity in which a defendant was sued without prior leave of court. The brief, settled by Chief J.S. Okutepa, SAN, the ADC’s lead counsel in the appeal against the amendment ruling, seeks to set aside the order and have the outstanding jurisdictional objection considered. The ADC also argued that Justice Lifu proceeded to judgment on the basis of an amended court process that was already the subject of an appeal, before the appellate court had determined whether the amendment was properly granted. The party warned that allowing INEC to act on the November 5 judgment before the appeal is resolved could create changes that would be difficult to reverse, even if the ADC eventually succeeds. “These are serious questions before the Court of Appeal. item.title: APC accuses ADC, NDC of sponsoring violence at rallies
item.description: The All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council has accused opposition parties, the African Democratic Congress (ADC) and Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), of allegedly sponsoring violence and orchestrating protests at its campaign rallies ahead of the 2027 general elections. The council also alleged that the opposition parties were using artificial intelligence-generated images, deepfakes, fake news and other propaganda techniques to manipulate public opinion against President Bola Tinubu and the APC. The allegations were contained in a statement issued on Tuesday by the council’s spokesperson, Dele Alake. The council recalled that ahead of the flag-off of its presidential campaign rally in Kaduna on October 24, it had warned Nigerians about what it described as plans by opposition elements to create tension, promote disharmony and introduce violence into political campaigns. It alleged that the ADC and NDC had devised strategies involving sponsored protests and misinformation to portray widespread public discontent against the Tinubu administration. The APC campaign council further alleged that opposition elements were mobilising young Nigerians to disrupt its rallies by chanting ‘Bamaiyi’ and carrying banners. It cited an incident at a mosque in Abuja last Friday, alleging that some protesters threw stones at the presidential motorcade. The council commended security personnel attached to the presidential convoy for exercising restraint during the incident. It also praised Tinubu for directing the Abuja Police Command to release those detained in connection with the incident. The statement further expressed concern over alleged attacks and threats against some APC members and supporters in the South-East, claiming that they were being labelled saboteurs for not supporting the NDC presidential candidate, Peter Obi. It also alleged that APC campaign billboards were being destroyed by individuals sponsored by opposition elements. The council described the alleged incidents as unacceptable, insisting that the country’s democratic space should remain open to all political parties and candidates. Reaffirming its position on peaceful political campaigns, the APC campaign council said it supported credible, free and fair elections across the country. It urged leaders of the ADC and NDC to desist from allegedly mobilising young Nigerians for activities that could expose them to danger. The council also called on political parties to conduct their campaigns peacefully and allow Nigerians to freely support candidates of their choice. item.title: Reps to probe 22 States over unpaid pensions
item.description: By Gift ChapiOdekina, Abuja The House of Representatives has resolved to investigate the failure of 22 states to pay retirement benefits regularly, following concerns that thousands of elderly pensioners are being abandoned to hunger, poverty and preventable deaths. The resolution was sequel to a motion of urgent public importance sponsored by Rep. Adesola Adebayo, representing Apapa Federal Constituency of Lagos State, on Tuesday at plenary. Moving the motion, Rep. Adebayo cited a report indicating that only 14 of Nigeria’s 36 states pay pensions regularly, while the remaining 22 owe retirees several months or, in some cases, several years of entitlements. He described pensions as an earned right rather than a privilege or charity, stressing that retirees who had devoted between 30 and 35 years to public service deserved to enjoy their benefits without unnecessary hardship. The lawmaker expressed concern that many pensioners aged between 70 and 90 were dying in poverty because they could not afford food, medication, rent and other basic necessities. He also raised concerns over the practice of subjecting elderly retirees to prolonged verification exercises, forcing some to queue for days under harsh weather conditions, with reports of pensioners collapsing and dying in the process. Adebayo argued that the non-payment of pensions amounted to a violation of constitutional provisions and human dignity, while creating fear among serving public workers who could begin to see retirement as a death sentence. The motion, however, generated disagreements among lawmakers over the constitutional powers of the National Assembly to intervene in pension matters involving state governments. Rep. item.title: A vote for Tinubu will translate into preservation of the North – Shettima
item.description: Vice President Kashim Shettima has called on the people of the North to vote massively for the re-election of President Bola Tinubu on January 16, 2027. Shettima made the call on Tuesday in Birnin Kebbi during the All Progressives Congress (APC) Campaign Rally, held at Haliru Abdu Stadium in Kebbi. The vice president stated that a vote for President Tinubu and VP Shettima would be a vote for the preservation of the North. “We are grateful that the North kept its promise in 2023. The North repaid Tinubu’s kindness and support for late former President Muhammadu Buhari. “We are even more grateful that you are prepared to do the same in January 2027. You have rejected the lies, the distortions. “And the half-truths, the taunts, the insinuations, the threats and the noise of the opposition. We are here because you can see through them. “A vote for His Excellency, President Bola Tinubu, and for me as your Vice President is a vote for the preservation of the North,” he said. On security, Shettima said President Tinubu increased the salaries of the armed forces by up to 80 per cent and prioritised the welfare of all security agencies. “He also understands the needs of our farmers. Thousands of you participated in our dry-season programme to grow rice, maize and cassava. “That is why we have continued to supply you with the equipment you need. “Of the superhighway we are building from Sokoto to Badagry to ease movement across the country, 258 kilometres run through Kebbi. That is the longest stretch in any state,” the VP added. Shettima said Tinubu’s administration also undertook repairs on the Jega-Koko-Yauri and Birnin Kebbi-Argungu federal roads to ease journeys. “But roads alone are not enough without electricity. “We have increased the capacity of the Birnin Kebbi transmission substation while constructing a 3.5-megawatt solar project in Ambursa to serve homes and businesses,” he said. On healthcare, he said the Renewed Hope administration of Tinubu upgraded the Federal Medical Centre in Birnin Kebbi to a teaching hospital. “While primary healthcare centres across the state receive federal support through the Basic Health Care Provision Fund. “We have also invested in the skills of your young people. “Mr. President’s economic reforms have increased the revenue available to states to fund their initiatives and projects,” Shettima revealed. The Vice President said that Kebbi, like other states, struggled to fund its projects. He assured that the administration would not rest until every kobo earned and saved through “these reforms is invested in your welfare. “This is why we have come again: to continue what we started about three years ago. “On 16 January 2027, I trust you to come out en masse and vote for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu. “On 6 February 2027, I trust you to return Gov. item.title: NDC alleges N11.2trn Pipeline Security bill exceeds Military budget
item.description: Says President Tinubu Presides oover Opaque N11,2 trillion Pipeline Security bill that Doubles the Entire military budget while Starving of Armed Forces, Security continues to escalate By Henry Umoru ABUJA- The Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC has the alarm that President Bola Tinubu’s administration is presiding over what it termed, an opaque N11.2 trillion pipeline security expenditure, alleging that the amount exceeds Nigeria’s entire defence and security budget. According to the party, the figure was contained in the audited financial disclosures of the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPCL), which reportedly showed N11.2 trillion in “other receivables from the Federation” linked to energy security costs and what it described as unverified off-budget deductions. In a statement signed yesterday by the Spokesperson, NDC National Campaign Council, Dr. Chiogo Constance Ikokwu, NDC explained that the amount is more than twice the N4.91 trillion allocated to all defence and security agencies in the 2025 budget and over three times the ₦3.10 trillion appropriated to the Ministry of Defence for the Army, Navy and Air Force. The NDC further expressed concern over inadequate funding for military equipment, claiming that 75.9 per cent of the 2026 core defence budget of N3.15 trillion was allocated to personnel, while only 14.7 per cent, representing N464 billion, was earmarked for capital weapons as it further alleged that only seven per cent of the 2025 Defence Capital Budget was released, questioning the government’s commitment to adequately equipping the armed forces. The NDC while calling for what it described as an immediate forensic audit of the ₦11.2 trillion NNPCL energy security balance to establish the amounts paid to private contractors and those arising from legacy deductions, also asked for full disclosure of funds released for military capital equipment and troop welfare in 2025 and 2026. Ikokwu who questioned the reason for the expenditure at a time when insecurity, including kidnapping, killings and ransom payments, continues to threaten communities across the country, alleged that the huge pipeline security bill raised questions about transparency and accountability in the management of public resources, describing the expenditure as a possible political patronage fund disguised as energy security. Ikokwu urged Nigerians to vote for the Peter Obi/ Rabiu Kwankwaso ticket to dismantle the criminal system in Nigeria, adding that the ticket believes that Nigeria must work for all, and not a few. item.title: Tinubu Approves Establishment Of Kebbi Inland Dry Port
item.description: President Bola Tinubu has approved the establishment of an inland dry port in Kebbi State as part of efforts to boost economic activities and improve trade in the state. The President announced the approval on Tuesday during the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally in Birnin Kebbi, the state capital. He also pledged to approve additional road infrastructure projects for the state following requests by Governor Nasir Idris. The rally, held at the Birnin Kebbi Stadium, attracted thousands of APC supporters who gathered to express their support for Tinubu’s re-election bid ahead of the 2027 presidential election. Vice President Kashim Shettima and other party leaders were also present at the event, which featured speeches and goodwill messages from party chieftains. ﻿ Speaking at the rally, Governor Idris expressed satisfaction with the turnout and pledged that Kebbi State would deliver 100 per cent of its votes to Tinubu in the 2027 election. Also addressing the crowd, the Director-General of the APC Presidential Campaign Council, Senator Abdulazeez Yari, said the President had done much for the North-West, including Kebbi State. Yari attributed the large turnout to Tinubu’s acceptance in the region, citing the Sokoto-Badagry Superhighway project, which he said would pass through more than 200 kilometres of Kebbi State. In his remarks, Shettima urged residents of the North to support Tinubu’s re-election, recalling the President’s support for the late President Muhammadu Buhari, who governed Nigeria for eight years. He said Tinubu had stood by Buhari during his political journey and throughout his administration. Taking the podium, Tinubu thanked the people of Kebbi for their support and commended Governor Idris for his leadership. He subsequently announced the approval of some federal projects requested by the governor, including the establishment of the Kebbi Inland Dry Port. The rally also featured goodwill messages from the Speaker of the House of Representatives, the Deputy President of the Senate and other APC leaders and supporters. item.title: ‎FG launches CNG stations in four varsities
item.description: By Chidi Ndaa ‎TO ease the transport challenges of varsity students, staff and host communities, the Federal Government on Tuesday inaugurated Compressed Natural Gas Stations in four universities. The CNG stations are located at the University of Uyo (Akwa Ibom State), University of Nsukka (Enugu State), Federal University of Petroleum Resources, Effurun (Delta State), and the University of Calabar (Cross River State). ‎The Minister of State, Petroleum Resources (Gas), Ekperikpe Ekpo, said the scheme was aimed at ensuring that students, staff and members of the host communities enjoyed cheap transportation to their various destinations. Ekpo, who launched the scheme at UNIUYO, added that CNG was generally cheaper than petrol and diesel, offering motorists within the communities the opportunity to spend less on cleaner fuel. The minister hailed President Bola Tinubu for his (Tinubu) Renewed Hope Agenda, which has placed natural gas at the heart of the country’s economic renewal programme. Ekpo disclosed that the President had also approved the Special Palliative Relief on University Transportation Programme. According to him, the programme is in line with the 20 Universities CNG Ecosystem Initiative to mitigate the effect of petroleum subsidy reform on students and staff. He said, “For students, young people who earn a living from commercial transport, and vulnerable members of society who depend on public transport, these savings mean lower transport costs and more money kept in their pockets for education, enterprise, food and other household needs.” “The benefits of adopting CNG for mobility are practical and immediate. CNG is generally cheaper than petrol and diesel, so vehicle owners, commercial drivers and transport operators spend less on fuel. ‎“Under the watch of Mr President, gas is no longer a resource we merely flare or export; it is a resource we are using to power our vehicles, create jobs and put money back in the pockets of our people.”. item.title: Single Window: Nigeria’s $6.1bn non-oil exports drive fresh trade reforms
item.description: By Obas Esiedesa, Abuja The Federal Government on Tuesday disclosed that it is set to streamline export documentation and regulatory approvals from December 14, 2026, as part of efforts to sustain growth in Nigeria’s non-oil exports, which hit a record $6.1bn in 2025. The reform, under the second phase of the National Single Window project, is expected to eliminate multiple documentation processes, reduce bureaucratic bottlenecks and lower the cost of exporting Nigerian products. The Director of the National Single Window Project, Tola Fakolade, disclosed this at a stakeholders’ engagement in Abuja, saying the export-focused phase would provide businesses with a single digital platform for processing regulatory licences, permits and certificates. He explained that the platform would enable exporters to submit required documents through one entry point rather than visiting different government agencies to obtain multiple approvals. Fakolade said the first phase of the project, which focused on import licences and certificates, had processed more than 169,000 licences, certificates and permits since its launch. He added that feedback from users had helped improve the platform, while lessons from the import phase would guide the implementation of the export component. The initiative comes as Nigeria’s non-oil export earnings increased by 11.5 per cent to a record $6.1bn in 2025, while export volume rose by 10 per cent to 8.02 million metric tonnes. The Executive Director and Chief Executive Officer of the Nigerian Export Promotion Council, NEPC, Nonye Ayeni, who disclosed the figures, said the country exported 281 products to 120 countries, including 36 African nations. Ayeni, however, warned that sustaining the growth would require addressing trade procedures and regulatory delays, which she identified as major challenges confronting exporters. She said exporters often had to visit several government offices, submit identical documents repeatedly and secure multiple approvals before their goods could leave the country. According to her, such delays sometimes result in contract cancellations, increased business costs and deterioration of perishable products, leading to rejection by international buyers. She said the National Single Window would address the challenges by connecting relevant government agencies to a centralised digital platform for submitting, processing and approving trade documents. Ayeni disclosed that NEPC was working with the National Single Window Secretariat to integrate its export certification registration process, currently operated through the council’s e-registration portal, into the platform. She added that the council was also working to connect its Export Expansion Grant platform through an application programming interface to facilitate seamless processing and eliminate the movement of physical documents between institutions. item.title: I contemplated suicide at height of Man United career, Rooney reveals
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Wayne Rooney has revealed he contemplated suicide during the height of his Manchester United career, despite success on the pitch and major milestones in his personal life. Speaking on the Life At The Midpoint with Gabby Logan podcast, the former England captain said he struggled with his mental health, spent two days at a time drinking at home and withdrew from people around him. “I can look back and say I was selfish, but I knew I was going through something which I was really struggling to deal with,” Rooney said. “Then I didn’t want Kai seeing me like that, so that’s why I’d hide away as well. “I got to a place where you’re contemplating suicide. You just didn’t want to be around anyone. I didn’t want to see people in the streets. I didn’t want to go into shops. “I was always comfortable on a football pitch, but everything else (I) really struggled with it.” Rooney, Manchester United’s all-time record goalscorer with 253 goals, said he found it difficult to admit he was struggling because he feared it would be seen as a sign of weakness. “You don’t want to show any weakness, so you try to mask it,” he said. “Even though I knew the position I was in, it was difficult to actually admit that I was in that position because I felt like you feel less of a man if you like for doing that. “I was speaking to a therapist to try and figure out what was up with me because, when I look back, I was probably at the height of my career, I’ve just had a young son, I’ve just been married. It should be the happiest point in my life, and it wasn’t. “It was probably the lowest point because of the selfish acts I was taking.” Rooney, who married Coleen in 2008 and became a father to their first child, Kai, the following year, credited his wife with helping him through the period. “Coleen helped me massively. She could have walked away, it was that bad, but she stuck by me and helped me get through it,” he said. Rooney left Manchester United in 2017 and later had spells with Everton, DC United and Derby County. His last managerial role was at Plymouth Argyle, which he left in December 2024. item.title: 2027: We’ll never disappoint you — Kebbi governor assures Tinubu
item.description: Kebbi State Governor, Nasir Idris, has assured President Bola Tinubu that the state will remain loyal to the All Progressives Congress (APC) and deliver overwhelming support for his re-election in the 2027 presidential election. Idris gave the assurance on Tuesday while welcoming Tinubu to the state during the APC campaign rally, saying Kebbi had consistently supported the President and would do even more in the forthcoming election. “Mr President, Kebbi State has never disappointed you, and we will never disappoint you. In 2023, we gave you total support. In this election, we will give you even more,” the governor said. He added, “I assure you that Kebbi State will deliver APC 100 per cent by God’s grace.” The governor described the large turnout at the rally as evidence of the state’s support for Tinubu and his running mate, Vice-President Kashim Shettima. “This massive crowd you see here is a clear testimony that Kebbi State is APC and Kebbi State is for Bola Ahmed Tinubu and Kashim Shettima,” he said. Idris also commended the President for what he described as his administration’s interventions in the state, particularly in agriculture, infrastructure, education, healthcare and security. He thanked Tinubu for the Renewed Hope Agenda and support for farmers, which he said had contributed to a rice revolution in Kebbi. “We thank you for the roads, for the schools, for the hospitals, and for security support you give us,” he said. The governor said his administration had also invested in strengthening the state’s security architecture, improving health facilities, providing free agricultural inputs to farmers and constructing rural and township roads across the state. According to him, the investments have helped farmers work with confidence, created employment opportunities for young people and supported the empowerment of women. Idris, however, used the occasion to appeal to Tinubu to facilitate the full operationalisation of the Samia Inland Dry Port in Bagoro Local Government Area of the state. He said the facility, when fully operational, would boost revenue generation, create jobs and promote economic growth in Kebbi. item.title: Super Eagles held to dissapointing goalless draw by Tanzania in AFCON qualifier
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye The Super Eagles of Nigeria were held to a 0-0 draw by Tanzania on Tuesday, missing the chance to strengthen their Africa Cup of Nations qualifying campaign. Eric Chelle’s side had more possession and created several chances but could not find a way past the hosts’ defence in 90 minutes. The Super Eagles started brightly, with Moses Usor seeing an effort blocked inside the opening 15 minutes. Fisayo Dele-Bashiru also tested Tanzania with a shot from outside the penalty area, while Tolu Arokodare fired wide in the 35th minute. Tanzania remained a threat after the break, with Kibu Denis and Iddi Selemani both missing opportunities to put their side ahead. Nigeria continued to press, but Akor Adams sent an effort wide from the centre of the penalty area in the 70th minute. Arokodare later came close with a left-footed attempt from inside the box, but his shot also failed to hit the target. Tanzania nearly snatched a late winner when a speculative effort from the edge of the area struck the post. Alhassan Yusuf then tried to release a forward with a through ball, but the move was stopped for offside. Nigeria could not find a breakthrough in the closing minutes as Tanzania held on for a point. Nigeria will now hope Madagascar defeat Guinea-Bissau in Group L to keep their qualification hopes alive. Eric Chelle’s side had claimed a 3-1 victory over Tanzania in Friday’s first leg at the Godswill Akpabio International Stadium in Uyo. Alhassan Yusuf scored the opener before Tolu Arokodare struck twice after the break. The Super Eagles went into Tuesday’s match with six points from three games, one point behind Group L leaders Guinea-Bissau, who had played out a 1-1 draw with Madagascar in their previous fixture. Tanzania had already qualified for the tournament as one of the co-hosts, leaving Nigeria, Guinea-Bissau and Madagascar to battle for the group’s other qualification spot. Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda will jointly host the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations from June 19 to July 17. item.title: Radda Warns Against ‘419 Politicians’ As Supporters Rally For APC In Katsina
item.description: Katsina State Governor, Malam Dikko Umaru Radda, has urged voters to reject what he described as “419 politicians” in the 2027 general elections, declaring that only leaders with proven records of service deserve the people’s mandate. The governor appealed on Tuesday during the Tinubu/Dikko 2027 Campaign Council rally at the Mai’adua International Border Market in Mai’adua Local Government Area, where thousands of APC supporters gathered as the campaign tour continued across the Daura Senatorial Zone. Addressing the enthusiastic crowd, Governor Radda said the massive turnout reflected public confidence in his administration’s performance, particularly in healthcare delivery, education, teacher recruitment, youth empowerment and other development programmes. Supporters rally for Tinubu in Katsina State. He expressed appreciation to the people of Mai’adua for their overwhelming support and pledged to consolidate on the achievements of his administration if re-elected. “We have nothing to say but to thank God for the people of Mai’adua. We are grateful for the support we have received from women, youths and the elderly. This massive turnout shows that the people are satisfied with our achievements and leadership, especially in healthcare, education, teacher recruitment and empowerment.» “Please don’t make the mistake of electing 419 politicians. I know you are not in support of such politicians, and by the grace of God, we will reciprocate this confidence if re-elected. You have also demonstrated that you are genuine supporters and true admirers of the late President Muhammadu Buhari.” The governor also welcomed thousands of defectors from the African Democratic Congress (ADC) into the All Progressives Congress (APC), describing the development as further evidence of the ruling party’s growing popularity across the state. The rally’s highlight was the presentation of an Award of Excellence to Governor Radda by health workers in Mai’adua Local Government Area in recognition of what they described as his transformative leadership and commitment to strengthening the state’s healthcare sector. Earlier, Governor Radda commissioned the newly constructed Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC) Dumurkul Division in Mai’adua Local Government Area. The security facility was built by the Chairman of Mai’adua Local Government, Hon. Mamman Salisu Na-Allahu, as part of efforts to strengthen grassroots security and enhance the fight against insecurity in the border communities. Commissioning the project, Governor Radda commended the council chairman for his foresight and commitment to safeguarding lives and property, stressing that security remains the cornerstone of his administration’s development agenda.
